When someone does something for us, gives us a gift, or provides an unrequested service, we instinctively feel indebted and compelled to reciprocate, often with something of greater value. For example, if a company offers you a free sample, you might feel more inclined to buy their product later. Understanding this principle highlights how deeply ingrained social exchange is in human interaction and why giving first can be such an effective tool in building relationships, trust, and influence, but also how it can be subtly exploited.

Understanding the FAE encourages empathy and helps us avoid quick, often unfair, judgments of others, prompting us to consider the broader context behind their actions.
